# Periodic table of the elements (`periodic_table`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/chemistry.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Chemistry (`chemistry`)
- Deps: needs atomic_theory; helped by molecules_mole_concept, spectrum_colour, atomic_structure
- Core idea: When the elements are listed in order of atomic weight, similar properties recur at regular intervals, so they can be set out in rows and columns in which each column is a family (lithium, sodium, potassium; chlorine, bromine, iodine). Gaps in the table are undiscovered elements whose properties can be predicted from their neighbours. The true ordering principle is the number of positive charges in the nucleus, not the weight.
- Pitfalls:
  - Saying Mendeleev alone found it; Newlands, Lothar Meyer and others had versions, and his distinction is the bold predictions.
  - Ordering strictly by weight; a few pairs (tellurium and iodine) must be swapped.
  - Trying it with wrong atomic weights from before Cannizzaro; the pattern does not appear.
  - Forgetting that the whole column of noble gases was unknown until the 1890s.
- History: europe: 1817–1829 Döbereiner's triads; 1865 Newlands' octaves; 1869 Mendeleev and 1870 Lothar Meyer publish periodic systems; gallium (1875), scandium (1879) and germanium (1886) confirm the predictions; 1913 Moseley orders the elements by atomic number
- Read:
  - Eric R. Scerri, The Periodic Table: Its Story and Its Significance (2007)
  - J. W. van Spronsen, The Periodic System of Chemical Elements: A History of the First Hundred Years (1969)
